title_en: Beijing Film Audio & Video Recording Company v. Beijing Film Academy — dispute over infringement of exclusive right to use a work
keywords_en: civil; copyright infringement dispute; first instance; basic people's court; Beijing; legal person; Copyright Law; determination of fair use; scope of exclusive right of use; boundary between educational use and commercial use; partial support; transfer of adaptation right of a novel; filming of student graduation works; participation in international film festival; dispute over college's infringement of exclusive right to use a work
full_text_en:
Beiyin Audio & Video Recording Company v. Beijing Film Academy

— dispute over infringement of exclusive right to use a work

Plaintiff: Beiyin Audio & Video Recording Company.

Legal representative: Li Baoping, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Ma Xiaogang, attorney at Junhe Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Wang Ying, officer of Beiyin Audio & Video Recording Company.

Defendant: Beijing Film Academy.

Legal representative: Liu Guodian, President of the Academy.

Agent ad litem: Han Bing, attorney at Beijing Economic Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Hou Keming, officer of Beijing Film Academy.

The plaintiff, Beiyin Audio & Video Recording Company, filed an action with the Haidian District People's Court of Beijing against the defendant, Beijing Film Academy, for a dispute over infringement of the exclusive right to use a work.

The plaintiff, Beiyin Audio & Video Recording Company, alleged: In March 1992, the writer Wang Zengqi transferred to the plaintiff the right to adapt his novel *Shou Jie* (The Vow) into a film or television drama and the right to produce such a work. The parties renewed the contract in December 1994, with a term valid until March 1998. Under the contract, the plaintiff is the sole lawful holder of the adaptation and production rights for the novel *Shou Jie*. In preparation for filming the work, the plaintiff had completed preliminary work and invested considerable human and material resources. On January 14, 1995, the plaintiff read in the *Drama and Film News* (Issue No. 729) a report entitled "*Shou Jie* Shortlisted for the French Short Film Festival." From this, the plaintiff learned that the Beijing Film Academy, without permission from the rights holder, had adapted and produced a film based on the novel *Shou Jie*, and had organized a delegation to take the film to the Langlois International Student Film Festival in France, where it was shortlisted for the Clermont-Ferrand Film Festival. The Beijing Film Academy openly infringed the plaintiff's exclusive right to adapt the work, extending its infringing conduct from within the school to outside, and from domestic to international, causing the plaintiff irreparable mental and property losses. Therefore, the plaintiff requested the court to order the Beijing Film Academy to cease the infringement, destroy the infringing film copies, publicly apologize to the plaintiff, compensate the plaintiff for economic losses of RMB 200,000 (taking into account the defendant's financial situation), reimburse all expenses incurred by the plaintiff in this case, and bear the litigation costs.

The defendant, Beijing Film Academy, argued: The film *Shou Jie* adapted and produced by the class of 1989 students was a graduation assignment. Before filming, the defendant had sought the plaintiff's opinion, and the plaintiff did not expressly object. The defendant's act of filming was a fair use of Mr. Wang Zengqi's published work *Shou Jie*, with the direct purpose of producing a student graduation project, and did not infringe the plaintiff's exclusive right to use the work. The defendant took *Shou Jie* and other student films to the Langlois Student Film Festival in France, whose theme was "Tribute to Beijing Film Academy." *Shou Jie* is a short film of only 30 minutes. Apart from one screening in the defendant's small theater for teaching observation, it was screened only once at the Langlois Student Film Festival. The Langlois Film Festival is not a pre-selection festival for the Clermont-Ferrand Film Festival. In short, the defendant had no ill intent in producing *Shou Jie*, and in fact did not participate in the Clermont-Ferrand Film Festival. The plaintiff's claim that the defendant "extended its infringing result from within the school to outside, and from domestic to international" is an unfounded exaggeration, and the assertion of "irreparable mental and property losses" is alarmist. The plaintiff's lawsuit, based on neither factual basis nor correct understanding of the law, has seriously damaged the defendant's reputation and caused irreparable harm in society. The defendant requested the court to dismiss the plaintiff's claims.

After trial, the Haidian District People's Court found: On May 5, 1992, the plaintiff, Beiyin Audio & Video Recording Company (Party B), entered into a contract with Wang Zengqi (Party A), which stipulated: "1. Party A permits Party B to adapt into film or television and produce the works *Shou Jie*, *Da Nao Ji Shi* (Chronicles of the Great Lake), and *Tu* (Apprentice) to which Party A holds the copyright. 2. Party A guarantees that within three years, it will not transfer the adaptation and production rights of the above three works to others. The term is from March 15, 1992 to March 15, 1995." The contract also provided: "Party B shall pay Party A a one-time adaptation transfer fee of RMB 5,000. If Party B fails to adapt and produce the above three works before the expiration of the contract term, it shall lose its adaptation and production rights. To reacquire such rights, Party B must renegotiate with Party A." On December 30, 1994, Beiyin Audio & Video Recording Company and Wang Zengqi renewed the contract regarding the film and television adaptation and production of *Shou Jie*, *Da Nao Ji Shi*, and *Tu*. The renewed contract added the following clause: "Party A guarantees that within three years, it will not transfer the adaptation and production rights of the above three works to others. The term is from March 15, 1995 to March 15, 1998. Party B shall pay Party A an adaptation rights transfer fee of RMB 5,000. After the film is completed, Party B shall pay Party A an additional transfer fee of RMB 5,000, for a total of RMB 10,000." In October 1992, Wu Qiong, a student in the Literature Department of Beijing Film Academy, adapted Wang Zengqi's novel *Shou Jie* into a film script as a course assignment. After reviewing the adaptation assignments submitted by students, Beijing Film Academy selected Wu Qiong's script *Shou Jie* for the production of a graduation film. Wu Qiong and Zhao Fengxi, a faculty member at Beijing Film Academy, contacted Wang Zengqi by telephone. Wang Zengqi stated that the adaptation and production rights for the novel *Shou Jie* had been transferred to Beiyin Audio & Video Recording Company. Zhao Fengxi consulted with Beiyin Audio & Video Recording Company, which did not expressly consent to Beijing Film Academy’s filming of *Shou Jie*. In April 1993, Beijing Film Academy invested RMB 50,000 and organized students of the class of 1989 to jointly produce the film *Shou Jie*. Filming was completed in May 1993. The film is 30 minutes long, shot on 16mm film, with opening credits stating "Adapted from Wang Zengqi's novel of the same title" and closing credits stating "Beijing Film Academy Production." After completion, the film was screened once in the small theater of Beijing Film Academy for teaching observation, with an audience of faculty and students of the Academy. In November 1994, with approval from the Ministry of Radio, Film and Television, Beijing Film Academy organized a delegation to take *Shou Jie* and other films to the Langlois International Student Film Festival in France. The film *Shou Jie* was screened at that festival, with an audience consisting of students and faculty from various countries attending the festival, as well as local citizens. During the screening, the festival organizing committee sold a small number of tickets to the public. Beijing Film Academy did not participate in the Clermont-Ferrand Film Festival. Beijing Film Academy produced two film copies of *Shou Jie*, one of which was sealed and kept at the Academy, and the other was in transit from the Langlois Film Festival organizing committee to Beijing Film Academy. Beijing Film Academy also made one videotape of *Shou Jie*, which was also sealed at the Academy.

The above facts are confirmed by: the statements of both parties; the contract for the adaptation and production rights of the novel *Shou Jie* signed between Wang Zengqi and Beiyin Audio & Video Recording Company; the film script *Shou Jie* adapted by Wu Qiong; the shooting script by the film's director; the official approval document of the Ministry of Radio, Film and Television titled "Report on the Selection and Screening of Films for the Langlois Film Festival Organizing Committee at Beijing Film Academy"; one film copy of *Shou Jie*; and one videotape, among other evidence.

The Haidian District People's Court held: The exclusive right to adapt the novel *Shou Jie* by means of filming a television drama or a film, which the plaintiff Beiyin Audio & Video Recording Company lawfully acquired through contract, is protected by law. Without permission from the holder of such exclusive right, no other person may adapt or use the work in the same manner; otherwise, such conduct constitutes infringement of the exclusive right. Article 22, paragraph 1, item (6) of the Copyright Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Translation or reproduction in small quantities of a published work for use by teaching or scientific research personnel in classroom teaching or scientific research, provided that the work is not published or distributed." Such acts "may be done without permission from, and without payment of remuneration to, the copyright owner, provided that the name of the author and the title of the work are indicated, and the other rights enjoyed by the copyright owner under this Law are not infringed." The defendant Beijing Film Academy, based on actual teaching needs, selected the classroom exercise work of student Wu Qiong—a film script adapted from Wang Zengqi's novel *Shou Jie*—and organized graduating students to produce a graduation film for the purpose of evaluating student learning outcomes. Although the adaptation of the script and the production of the film were done without permission from the exclusive right holder of the novel *Shou Jie*—the plaintiff Beiyin Audio & Video Recording Company—the use of the completed work domestically was limited to teaching observation and evaluation within Beijing Film Academy, and the work was not released or distributed to the public domain. Therefore, at this stage, the defendant's act of producing the film fell within the scope of fair use of another's work and did not constitute infringement of the plaintiff's lawfully acquired exclusive right to use the novel *Shou Jie*. However, in November 1994, Beijing Film Academy sent the film *Shou Jie* to France for the Langlois International Student Film Festival. When the film was screened at that festival, the audience included not only specific students and teachers but also local citizens, and the organizing committee sold a small number of tickets. This exceeded the scope of classroom teaching within the school, violated the provisions of the Copyright Law, and constituted infringement of the plaintiff's lawfully acquired exclusive right to use the novel *Shou Jie*. Beijing Film Academy shall apologize to Beiyin Audio & Video Recording Company for its infringing act. Although the defendant's infringement may have potential market implications for the plaintiff's future use of the same work in the same manner, the infringement was minor in nature, and compensation shall be determined accordingly.

For these reasons, on May 18, 1995, the Haidian District People's Court rendered the following judgment:

1. Within ten days after this judgment takes effect, the defendant Beijing Film Academy shall make a written apology to the plaintiff Beiyin Audio & Video Recording Company (the content of the apology is subject to court review).

2. The film copy and videotape of *Shou Jie* produced by the defendant Beijing Film Academy shall, from the effective date of this judgment, be used only for teaching purposes within the Academy and shall not be made available to the public domain.

3. Within ten days after this judgment takes effect, the defendant Beijing Film Academy shall pay the plaintiff Beiyin Audio & Video Recording Company RMB 10,000 as compensation for economic losses.

The plaintiff Beiyin Audio & Video Recording Company, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, appealed to the First Intermediate People's Court of Beijing.

The appellant Beiyin Audio & Video Recording Company argued: The fair use of another's work for teaching purposes as provided in the Copyright Law is limited to classroom teaching, and the permitted uses are limited to translation or reproduction in small quantities. The original judgment's recognition of the appellee's act of producing a film as fair use has no legal basis. The original judgment not only fails to protect the lawful rights of the rights holder but will also cause serious consequences. It requested the second-instance court to confirm the appellee's infringement and order compensation of RMB 250,000.

The appellee Beijing Film Academy argued: The appellant does not have the legal qualification to produce films and therefore should not enjoy the right to produce a film based on the novel *Shou Jie*. The appellee's production of the film *Shou Jie* for teaching purposes and its screening within the school constitute fair use. The appellant's grounds of appeal are untenable. The Langlois International Student Film Festival is purely an academic activity; the appellee's sending the film *Shou Jie* to that festival for exhibition does not constitute publication or distribution and does not exceed the scope of fair use. The original judgment's finding of infringement lacks sufficient basis, and the order that *Shou Jie* may only be used within the Academy has no legal basis. The finding that the film festival organizing committee sold a small number of tickets is also inconsistent with the facts. The appellee sought to set aside the part of the original judgment concerning the appellee's infringement.

The First Intermediate People's Court of Beijing held: The appellant Beiyin Audio & Video Recording Company entered into a valid copyright licensing contract with the copyright owner of the novel *Shou Jie*. Under the contract, the appellant obtained an exclusive right to adapt the novel into a film or television work. Since the law imposes no restriction on the subject qualification for holding such a right, the appellee's argument that the appellant does not enjoy the exclusive right to produce a film based on *Shou Jie* cannot be sustained. Pursuant to Article 35 of the Implementing Regulations of the Copyright Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides: "A user who has obtained an exclusive right may exclude any other person, including the copyright owner, from using the work in the same manner. If the user wishes to license a third party to exercise the same right, permission must be obtained from the copyright owner, unless otherwise agreed in the contract." The appellant's exclusive right is protected by law, and the appellant has the right to exclude others from using the novel *Shou Jie* in the same manner of filming a film or television work.

The purpose of Article 22, paragraph 1, item (6) of the Copyright Law of the People's Republic of China is to permit schools to use another's work without compensation within a certain scope for classroom teaching, so as to ensure the smooth conduct of teaching activities. The appellee is an art academy that trains film professionals, and its teaching methods are relatively special; practicing film production is an essential part of its classroom teaching activities. The appellee's organization of graduating students to adapt the novel *Shou Jie* and produce a film was for the purpose of completing the students' graduation projects and developing their practical skills. The screening of the film within the school was for teaching observation and evaluation, both of which are necessary components of classroom teaching. Therefore, the appellee's acts within the above scope constitute fair use of the novel *Shou Jie* and do not infringe the appellant's exclusive right.

The appellee took the film *Shou Jie* to the Langlois International Film Festival, and when the film was screened at the festival, the audience included not only students and teachers from various countries attending the festival but also local citizens. The festival organizing committee also publicly sold a small number of tickets. This is confirmed by the court's records of interviews with Wang Weiguo, Vice President of Beijing Film Academy who attended the festival, and Qiu Huaiyang, director of the film *Shou Jie*. By taking the film *Shou Jie* to the film festival, the appellee allowed it to enter the public domain, exceeding the scope of use for classroom teaching within the school. This does not constitute fair use under the Copyright Law, infringes the appellant's exclusive right to use the novel *Shou Jie*, and has an adverse impact on the appellant's potential market for using the work in the same manner. The appellee shall be held liable for this.

In summary, the original judgment correctly found that the appellee's production of the film *Shou Jie* for classroom teaching constituted fair use, and correctly found that the appellee's taking the film to an international film festival constituted infringement. The appellant's grounds of appeal are insufficient and are not supported. Accordingly, pursuant to Article 153, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court rendered judgment on October 10, 1995:

Appeal dismissed; the original judgment is affirmed.

The litigation costs of first instance, RMB 5,510, shall be borne by Beiyin Audio & Video Recording Company in the amount of RMB 2,204 and by Beijing Film Academy in the amount of RMB 3,306. The litigation costs of second instance, RMB 5,510, shall be borne by Beiyin Audio & Video Recording Company.
